speakers.name: Dr John Morrison
speakers.title: Associate Professor of Criminology, Maynooth University; Co-Editor in Chief, Behavioral Sciences of Terrorism and Political Aggression
speakers.bio: Dr John Morrison is an Associate Professor of Criminology at Maynooth University, Ireland. He is co-Editor in Chief of the journal Behavioral Sciences of Terrorism and Political Aggression. With a multi-disciplinary background, John's research interests include organisational fragmentation, individual disengagement, and the role of trust in the psychology of terrorism.

title: The Filtering Role of Trust in the Process of Disengagement
description: In this webinar, Dr John Morrison will focus on the role which trust plays within the process of disengagement from violent extremism. Dr Morrison will utilise the Phoenix model of disengagement and deradicalisation as a basis for his presentation. This model includes the theme of (dis)trust as a filter variable. Dr Morrison will critically discuss the implication of this and how it can be integrated within appropriate CVE approaches, including consideration of the need to understand cross-cultural differences in the development and maintenance of trust, and how this may impact our approaches and understanding of disengagement processes.

title: Legacies of 9/11: 25 Years of Changing Global Security
description: A week-long series of panel discussions marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks, presented by the AVERT Research Network with partner organisations including ANU, Moonshot, Macquarie University, and the Institute for Strategic Dialogue. Each session is separately hosted and requires its own registration.

speakers.name: Viktoria Rösch
speakers.title: Research Associate, GERDEA and DEMOREG Projects, Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences
speakers.bio: Viktoria Rösch is a sociologist and research associate in the joint research projects GERDEA and DEMOREG at Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences. Her research focuses on far-right women, gender, and visual politics. She is a doctoral candidate at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and serves on the board of the Working Group Sociology of the Far Right within the German Sociological Association (DGS).

title: Bodies of Defence: Far-Right Women and Militant Femininities in Germany and Europe
description:
This webinar will explore how women in far-right movements across Germany and Europe use social media, particularly Instagram, to shape and promote far-right ideas and identities. It will examine how female influencers and networks from a range of far-right communities - including New Right groups, ethnonationalist movements, political parties, music scenes, and football supporter networks - use images to spread common messages and connect with one another across national borders.

The webinar will look at how these women combine themes of threat, protection, rebellion, and strength to portray themselves as defenders of the nation and Europe. It will also examine how these visual narratives are shared between countries, helping to increase the visibility and influence of far-right women across Europe. Rather than arguing that these images directly encourage violence, the webinar will explore how they reinforce ideas about conflict, sacrifice, enemies, and the need to defend society. It argues that while women have long played roles in far-right movements, social media has given them a much more prominent and influential public role in shaping the movement's identity and messaging.

title: AVERT National Research Symposium 2026 — Call for Proposals
description: AVERT is calling for proposals for its 2026 National Research Symposium, Youth and Extremism: Thresholds, Interventions, Connections, taking place 26–27 November 2026 at Macquarie University's City Campus, Sydney. Submissions are open for papers, panels, roundtables, and workshops addressing youth radicalisation and violent extremism.

speakers.name: Lydia Khalil
speakers.title: Senior Research Fellow, Alfred Deakin Institute; Project Director, Lowy Institute
speakers.bio: Lydia Khalil is a Senior Research Fellow at the Alfred Deakin Institute and a Project Director at the Lowy Institute. In her capacity at Deakin University, she also served as Co-Convenor of the AVERT Research Network and as liaison to the Research and Evaluation Working Group (REWG) of CVESC. As part of her work with the Lowy Institute, Lydia manages the Transnational Challenges Program and Digital Threats to Democracy Project.

speakers.name: Dr Keiran Hardy
speakers.title: Associate Professor, School of Criminology and Criminal Justice, Griffith University
speakers.bio: Dr Keiran Hardy is an Associate Professor in the School of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Griffith University and a member of the Griffith Criminology Institute. He is a recognised expert in counter-terrorism and national security law. He is the author of Law in Australian Society: An Introduction to Principles and Process (Routledge, 2024, 2nd ed.) and is currently undertaking a 3-year ARC Discovery Project on conspiracy extremism, focusing on sovereign citizen beliefs and behaviours, pseudolaw, and the impact of conspiracy extremism on families and communities.
